newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends weaker vs U.S. dlr, TWI stabilises.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends weaker vs U.S. dlr, TWI stabilises.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended weaker against the U.S. dollar on Thursday but stabilised on its Trade-Weighted Index.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6937/44 from its 0.6964/71 open, largely due to renewed U.S. dollar strength, having traded a 0.6938-70 range on the day.
The Trade-Weighted Index closed barely changed at 67.14.
Dealers, noting the New Zealand Monetary Conditions Index (MCI) had remained at around minus 80 basis points, expected index-related positions to have been put in place by now.
"People seem to be comfortable now that they have their MCI related positions in place," said one dealer.
Base support was expected at 0.6930, but anywhere over 0.6960 would see no shortage of sellers, said one dealer.
Stability in the TWI was put down to a slight rebound in dollar/yen, which ended locally at 115.20/25.
